title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve Board adopts final rule to strengthen the ability of government authorities to resolve in orderly way largest domestic and foreign banks operating in the United States
主要内容: On December 15, 2016, the Federal Reserve Board adopted a final rule to enhance the capacity of government authorities to resolve the failure of the largest domestic and foreign banks operating in the United States in an orderly manner. The rule applies to domestic firms designated as global systemically important banks (GSIBs) and the U.S. operations of foreign GSIBs. The objective is to minimize the systemic impact of a GSIB failure by imposing losses on investors rather than taxpayers, while ensuring critical operations continue. This is achieved by requiring GSIBs to maintain sufficient long-term debt that can be converted to equity during resolution, thereby providing a source of private capital to support the firm's operations. The rule mandates that long-term debt must survive the loss of a bank's equity and subsequent failure, and be convertible into new equity. Debt issued on or before December 31, 2016, will be grandfathered, allowing it to count toward a firm's long-term debt requirements despite certain contractual clauses. Debt issued after this date must fully comply with the rule. All firms are required to adhere to the rule by January 1, 2019.
